name: spaced-arrangement
summary: Construct an ordering of items such that no two items of the same category are within min_distance positions of each other, and prove it, exposed as an MCP server. A fifth problem shape in this collection: combinatorial GENERATION under a guaranteed invariant, distinct from a single calculation, static constraint satisfaction, sequential action search, or structural graph algorithms. Solved via budgeted backtracking search (CSPRNG-randomized tie-breaking so repeated calls give different valid orderings; exhausting the search tree proves infeasibility instead of guessing), independently checked by verify_arrangement against the direct definition. As of this cycle, maximize_min_distance also finds the LARGEST min_distance achievable for a given items list (no caller-chosen value needed) via binary search over that same exhaustive feasibility proof, and proves the answer optimal -- structurally when it hits the n-1 ceiling, or via one more exhaustive search otherwise -- the rigorous formalization of 'spread categories as evenly as possible.'
problem: A uniformly random shuffle of a category-heavy list clusters same-category items together far more than people expect -- three songs by the same artist in a row reads as broken, not random. This is real and widely documented: Spotify and Apple both rewrote their shuffle algorithms specifically because of years of user complaints about exactly this (Spotify community forum threads, and Spotify's own 2026 engineering write-ups about generating hundreds of candidate shuffles and picking the best-spread one), and the general problem -- rearrange a multiset so no two equal items are within k positions of each other -- is a classic, named algorithmic problem (LeetCode 767 'Reorganize String', 621 'Task Scheduler', 358 'Rearrange String k Distance Apart') precisely because getting it right is easy to get plausibly-random-looking but actually wrong, especially once more than two categories interact (a per-category frequency check alone is necessary but not sufficient -- see the README/tests for a concrete counterexample). Search this cycle found no MCP server, keyless or otherwise, offering a generic 'arrange items under a minimum-spacing invariant, with a feasibility proof' tool -- existing Spotify-control MCP servers only toggle real Spotify's own shuffle mode, and existing pairwise/covering-array test-generation MCP servers (e.g. PictMCP) solve a different combinatorial-coverage problem, not spacing. This cycle's search for a NEW tool (interval/free-busy meeting-time-finding across timezones, general non-bipartite graph matching, rectangular/partial assignment) turned up nothing that cleared the saturation-or-sourced-need bar cleanly, so the cycle deepened this tool instead: its own README had explicitly flagged 'no soft spread-evenly-beyond-the-minimum mode' as a gap since it was built, and the same Spotify engineering write-up already cited as this tool's source describes generating many candidate shuffles and picking the best-spread one -- exactly what maximize_min_distance now does directly, with a formal optimality proof instead of picking-the-best-of-many-samples.
